script: No spread or total was saved, so this is form-only. JAX blitzes 39% and Drake Maye is better into pressure (0.09 EPA/dropback vs blitz, n=22, vs -0.06 with no blitz), so NE can stay on schedule with Rhamondre Stevenson (24 carries, 94 yards) and Treveyon Henderson (16/76) instead of a pass-heavy script. NE blitzes 38% into Trevor Lawrence at -0.40 EPA vs blitz (n=10), so Jacksonville's form script runs through Bhayshul Tuten (28 carries, 131 yards) rather than dropbacks.
who_goes_off: Stevenson should go off for NE: about 12 carries and 4 targets a game, 47 rush yards plus 23.5 receiving yards, into a JAX run defense allowing 4.13 YPC and a 39% blitz that feeds his -3 air-yard checkdowns. Tuten should go off for JAX: 14 carries and 65.5 rush yards a game at 4.68 YPC against a NE front allowing 4.30 YPC and 5 runs of 10-plus. Parker Washington (18 targets, 181 yards, 279 air yards) is the passing candidate, but NE has allowed only 4 passes of 20-plus on 70 attempts, so that deep-air profile is the fade.
weak_spot: JAX's hole is the middle, not the outside corners: 19.0 YPA on 7 middle attempts versus 7.86 left (28 att) and 7.78 right (18 att), so the matchup is linebackers, nickel, and safeties, and they have also allowed 8 passes of 20-plus on 58 attempts. NE is the same shape on a smaller scale, 10.69 YPA in the middle (13 att) against 4.48 left and 5.18 right, with only 4 explosives on 70 attempts, so outside shots to Brian Thomas Jr. (126 air yards, 80 receiving) are the wrong attack.
injury_fallout: No injury report was saved for NE@JAX, so nothing moves Stevenson, Henderson, Tuten, Washington, or the two-game target counts already on the sheet.
qb_vs_blitz: Maye beats the blitz at 0.09 EPA (n=22) against -0.06 with no blitz, and JAX brings it on 39% of dropbacks, which supports his 9 carries for 67 yards and the dump-offs to Stevenson (8 targets, -3 air yards, 47 receiving yards). Lawrence fails the blitz at -0.40 EPA (n=10) against 0.42 with no blitz, and NE blitzes 38%, so the Jacksonville answer is Tuten's 28 carries, not Lawrence's 4 rushes for 9 yards.

picks.why: Stevenson has 94 rush yards and 47 receiving yards over two games, about 70.5 scrimmage yards a game, against a 54 line. JAX allows 4.13 YPC and 5 runs of 10-plus, and their 39% blitz matches the checkdown role (8 targets, -3 air yards) that Maye's +0.09 blitz EPA keeps on the field.

Tuten has 28 carries for 131 yards (4.68 YPC), about 65.5 rush yards a game, against a 52 line, more than double Chris Rodriguez's 12 carries. NE allows 4.30 YPC and 5 runs of 10-plus, and Lawrence's -0.40 EPA vs a 38% NE blitz pushes that work onto Tuten instead of into dropbacks.
